text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- A plan to manufacture the world's first electronic wallet in Malaysia was unveiled in London on Wednesday.
-- The government is to build 80 new community centres nationwide, costing between 100,000 ringgit and two million ringgit each.

-- Malaysian Prime Minister said in London he hoped to increase the number of skilled workers to meet the needs of the Multimedia Super Corridor high-technology zone. The overall aim was to have adequate number of personnel to meet the information age requirement as Malaysia became a developed nation.
-- The local distributor of Harley-Davidson motorcycles plans to assemble the vehicles in Malaysia. It will be the first for the bikes outside the United States.
-- Malaysia moved up to the ninth place as the world's most competitive economy from tenth last year, according to the Global Competitiveness Report of the Geneva-based World Economic Forum.
